name: orla
description: Personal finance and small-business bookkeeping from your own books: your assistant books a bank statement after you check the rows, sorts expenses, reads budgets and net worth. It cannot move money.

interface.longDescription:
Hand your assistant a bank statement: it shows the rows it would book and why any would not, then books exactly those after your yes. Then ask where the money went last month, what is due this week, what you are worth today, who owes whom.

Orla keeps the books for people and small businesses whose money sits in more than one place: bank accounts, cards, cash, crypto wallets and exchanges, invoices out and bills in.

What your assistant can read: accounts and balances, transactions, categories, budgets against spending, net worth, shared expenses and who owes whom, supplier bills, payments waiting for a signature, and Orla's own reports, among them spending by category, bills due, VAT ahead, loans and debts. Cash forecast, receivables, payables and the other business reports come with Orla Pro; the rest works on a free account.

What your assistant can record: a transaction, a fix to its category, payee or note, a budget limit, a shared expense, an account kept by hand, a receipt or an invoice filed in your Documents, and the rows of a bank statement. To re-sort many transactions it first shows which rows would change, then applies exactly those, all or none. Amount, date and account cannot be edited.

It cannot move money. No payment, transfer or card tool is on this connection. In Orla, money leaves only by a payment or a mandate a person signed.

Card numbers, IBANs and wallet addresses come back masked to a short tail like 4417. On the consent screen you pick which spaces your assistant may see, and you can disconnect it at any time.

A free Orla account is enough to connect, and reading has no limit. Recording is counted in entries: 50 a month on Free, one per booked statement row. A longer statement books its newest rows, and your assistant says how many wait. A statement goes in as one file of up to 180 KB; reading it uses the space's monthly AI allowance (about four statements on Free). Orla's web app opens to new accounts a few at a time; your assistant works with a new account at once.
